key_facts.fact: Brief v2 on the same brains cut words per turn from 33.7/32.7 to 20.9/18.7, question-ending turns from 62%/76% to 13%/29%, stock phrases per call from 1.8/2.7 to 0.7/0, and abrupt hang-ups from 17-40% to 0.
key_facts.evidence: research/2026-10-20/voicelab/round1-review-and-v2.md and context/DIRECTION.md; text bake-off, 6 simulated callers x 10 turns per brain, 540 blind pairwise verdicts by GPT-4.1 and Gemini 3.8 Flash judges; simulated callers, no human round-2 ratings exist

key_facts.fact: Agenda ledger and hang-up guard are regex/lexicon based and written per scenario (told, offers, numbers dicts for renewal/support/follow-up/open) with Hindi-English cue, goodbye and closing lexicons; they must be generalised per client agent and per language before reuse.
key_facts.evidence: voicelab/server/persona_v2.py SCEN, ledger(), CUES, CLOSING, GOODBYE, hangup_ok()

key_facts.fact: Hang-up is honoured only when the reply contains a goodbye and the caller was not asking a question; audio must finish, then a 1.5 s beat, and it is cancelled if the caller speaks. S2S uses an end_call tool, cascades use an <end_call> marker.
key_facts.evidence: voicelab/server/calls.py end_after_playback, _after; persona_v2.py hangup_ok; GeminiLiveCall.setup

key_facts.fact: Turn-taking: server-side Silero VAD v5; reply released only after the final for the caller's latest speech segment, held 1.4 s after continuation words, unreleased reply withdrawn if the caller resumes, barge-in needs 2+ words or 700 ms, history truncated to what was heard. Across all stacks 15-42% of replies cut in on the caller and an elderly caller's 2.4 s pause was cut in on 100% of the time; target is at most 5% cut-ins at p50 gap at most 1.2 s.
key_facts.evidence: voicelab/server/calls.py CascadeCall._tick, incomplete(); voicelab/server/audio.py VAD; graph open.2026-10-19.turn-taking (lab round-1 data, small n)

key_facts.fact: Plivo phone leg ran 11 real calls in round 1 using G.711 mu-law 8 kHz bidirectional stream, 95-tap FIR resampling, clearAudio on barge-in, HMAC path-secret webhooks and missed-call number verification; it is a test rig on one trial number (credit about INR 764 expiring 2026-11-16, INR 80 monthly cap) with no DLT/DND/consent logic or concurrency.
key_facts.evidence: voicelab/server/phone.py; voicelab/README.md; context/DIRECTION.md open threads; research round1 review (65 calls: 54 browser, 11 phone)

key_facts.fact: Cost meter computes real per-component INR (ears by audio seconds sent, brain by tokens, voice by chars/audio tokens, live by usage metadata, phone by 60 s pulse at INR 95/USD) and streams it every 2 s; Plivo is shown but excluded from the AI spend cap. Pre-lab research stack quoted about INR 0.94/min; measured Gemini Live presets ran INR 4.2-5.7/min at 3-min calls.
key_facts.evidence: voicelab/server/calls.py add_cost/meter/cost_loop/summary; voicelab/server/catalog.py presets 'ref' column; rejected.2026-10-19.gemini-live-at-rs2

key_facts.fact: Relay's structural flaws: single JSON-blob entities table with raw SQL from 44+ files and CAS by full-JSON equality, no migrations, one org per user, hash-routed single page, 72-route action-string API, 7 long-running processes, no CRM objects (CSV Company/Country/Product columns had nowhere to go), customer CSV leaked into company-knowledge extraction, no outbound telephony.

key_facts.fact: Relay mechanisms worth re-implementing as concepts: evidence-span intake with exact-quote review, AI-assisted CSV column mapping (AI mapped name/email/phone/stage correctly in about 4.2 s; no heuristic auto-map existed), idempotent AI task router with run ledger and budgets, encrypted connector vault + OAuth + 19-adapter registry (check/read only, no tenant connected), durable delivery with uncertain states, agent version/release/rollback, public deployment boundary, auth and team roles.
